analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | today + factors + AI EPS tomorrow
key_insights: Industrials were at session highs, up 150bps in line with broader markets. Materials were closer to flat.
Technology and energy led the broader market and consumer staples fell the most. Data center led the industrial subsectors with aerospace also strong. Autos, airlines and agriculture lagged.
Crude was at its highs of the day, which the desk links to underperformance in oil-sensitive names.
Rates are holding at 4.99%. The dollar is at highs and attempting a breakout, which the desk flags as worth considering for exporters heading into 2027.
Macro watch list for the rest of the week is jobless claims, existing home sales and PPI.

Client inbounds cover the CARR move after its presentation, KBR weakness (analyst day or the tape), where data center appetite will sustainably return, the CNM pre-announcement, LMT strength versus other defense primes, and FLY feedback.
Three smaller-cap AI and data center names report tomorrow: FPS, LGN and DPC.

FPS pre-announced positively in late October after a CFO change, pointing to Q1 revenue and EBITDA at the higher end of or above guidance. The stock peaked at $65 in June and may have bottomed at $18 in early November.
LGN has beaten revenue by 10%+ and EBITDA by 20%+ in each of its four reported quarters since its September 2025 IPO. M&A has added to topline growth.
DPC is a less direct AI play that moves with the theme. Margins are the key KPI after declines despite 30%+ revenue growth in Q2.

Factors: today was the biggest outperformance of 12m momentum versus shorter-term momentum, with 3m and 6m momentum on record. AI and semis moves are now bleeding into 6m momentum, which sold off as recent losers rebounded. Factor moves and single-name moves are telling different stories.

market_movers.rationale: Pre-announced Q1 revenue and EBITDA at the higher end of or above guidance. Reports pre-market tomorrow with an 11am call. The desk will watch fiscal Q2 and full-year updates and the CFO transition.
Reports tomorrow after beating revenue by 10%+ and EBITDA by 20%+ in each of four prior quarters. The desk will look for updates on M&A, 2027 and the backlog.
Reports pre-market tomorrow for the second time since its summer IPO, with a 13% implied move. The desk will watch aerospace and IGT comments and margins.

sector_views.rationale: Up 150bps at session highs in line with the market, led by data center and aerospace. Autos, airlines and agriculture lagged.
Closer to flat on the day versus industrials up 150bps.

earnings_insights: FPS: pre-announced positively in late October (guidance pre-announcement, not a final print), implying Q1 revenue and EBITDA at the higher end of or exceeding company guidance. Reports fiscal Q2 pre-market tomorrow with an 11am call. A 3x+ book to bill is described as difficult to sustain but drives near-term estimates higher.

LGN: reports tomorrow. Has beaten revenue by 10%+ in each of the four quarters reported so far, with EBITDA beats of 20%+. The desk will look for updates on M&A and on 2027 and beyond given the backlog.

DPC: reports pre-market tomorrow, its second report as a public company. The stock moved up 4% after the first report and the implied move for tomorrow is 13%. Margins declined in Q2 despite 30%+ revenue growth.
risk_factors: FPS: a 3x+ book to bill is difficult to sustain, and the stock has been very volatile.
DPC: margins declined despite 30%+ revenue growth in Q2.
Crude at its highs of the day weighs on oil-sensitive names.
Factor moves and individual stock moves are diverging, so it is unclear whether the day is an unwind.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum factor: 12m momentum had its biggest outperformance versus shorter-term momentum, with both 3m and 6m momentum on record.
The composition of momentum is changing, as AI and semis moves bleed into 6m momentum, which sold off while recent losers rebounded.
DPC options imply a 13% move for tomorrow's report.
The dollar is at highs and attempting a breakout.
